title: Stationarity of Halted States
statement: Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, and fix an input bit string $x$. If an abstract state $s$ is halted, then running the program from $s$ for any $t\in\mathbb{N}$ leaves the state unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $R\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Lambda$ is a set of labels.
$P$ is a counter program over $R$ registers and labels in $\Lambda$.
An input bit string $x$ is fixed.
The abstract state $s$ has halted label.
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, $x$ an input bit
string, and $s$ an abstract state whose label component marks it as halted. Then for every
$t \in \mathbb{N}$, running $P$ on $x$ from $s$ for $t$ steps returns $s$ unchanged.
